Lessons.Title: Fractions and Whole Numbers
ExplanationParagraphs: 2021 warm-up Number Talk: Divide by 4 asks 12÷4, 24÷4, 60÷4 and 72÷4, yielding 3, 6, 15 and 18. Pupils mentally explain how familiar quotients, groups and place-value decomposition help with larger dividends. These are original integer division cases, not additional fraction labels.

2021 Activity 1, Fractions Located at Whole Numbers, assigns ONE list to EACH of three pupils in a group: ten halves 1/2 to 10/2; nine thirds 1/3 to 9/3; twelve fourths 1/4 to 12/4. Preserve all 31 source-assigned fractions and the separate horizontal 0-to-5 number-line comparisons. Do not collapse repeated representations of an integer across the lists or replace with a generic fraction simplification exercise.

Exactly eleven of the assigned original fractions are at whole numbers: from halves 2/2=1, 4/2=2, 6/2=3, 8/2=4, 10/2=5; from thirds 3/3=1, 6/3=2, 9/3=3; from fourths 4/4=1, 8/4=2, 12/4=3. There are other non-whole points between these. A fraction k/n reaches an integer only when its numerator is a multiple of the positive denominator; the whole-number location is then k/n.

Teacher-led grouping is part of the source activity: groups of three assign different denominator lists, independently label number lines, share strategies and identify aligned whole-number marks. The pattern across denominators is about counting equal-sized parts per WHOLE. The count of mathematically correct scalar positions does NOT certify the actual three produced diagrams or group explanations.

2021 Activity 2, Locate 1 on the Number Line, REVERSES the previous process: each originally supplied number line labels 0 and a first unit-fraction point (1/2, 1/4, 1/6 or 1/8), but not 1. Students ITERATE that provided unit-fraction length 2, 4, 6 or 8 times to construct and label 1. They explain their strategy, share with a partner, and then answer how to extend the same equal increments to locate 2. This is not a task where the endpoint 1 is given first.

For original source unit anchors: 1/2 requires two equal increments to reach 1 and four to reach 2; 1/4 requires four to reach 1 and eight to reach 2; 1/6 requires six and twelve; 1/8 requires eight and sixteen. These are exact mathematical checks, but the actual drawn extension, equal spacing and peer explanation require teacher review.

2021 synthesis invites comparison of whole-number labels as fractions, such as 1=2/2, 2=4/2 and 3=6/2, and how to use known unit positions to establish 1 and 2. Source Cool-down is titled Where is 1? but the publisher prompt is teacher-gated; Edulytics first-party tasks are independent and original graphics are not embedded.

KeyConcepts.Title: Whole numbers as fractions
KeyConcepts.Definition: A whole number can be represented by a fraction with numerator divisible by the denominator.
KeyConcepts.Rule: n whole units = (n×d)/d for any positive integer d.

KeyConcepts.Title: Aligned whole-number points
KeyConcepts.Definition: Different fraction partitions share the same whole-number locations on number lines with equal 0-to-1 reference lengths.
KeyConcepts.Rule: The nth count of 1/d reaches a whole precisely when the count is divisible by d.
KeyConcepts.Example: 4/4 and 3/3 are at the same coordinate 1.

KeyConcepts.Title: Reconstruct the unit from a fractional landmark
KeyConcepts.Definition: Knowing a first 1/d tick reveals the size of one fractional step.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Iterate d same-size intervals from zero to locate 1, and 2d intervals to locate 2.
KeyConcepts.Example: Starting with 1/6, six matching steps reach one.

KeyConcepts.Title: Source group tasks
KeyConcepts.Definition: Original activity distributes three different fraction lists to a group, one per learner.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Preserve the 10 halves, 9 thirds and 12 fourths and compare their positions.
KeyConcepts.Example: 2/2,3/3 and4/4 all locate the first whole.

WorkedExamples.Title: Original mental division warm-up
WorkedExamples.Question: Compute 12÷4,24÷4,60÷4,72÷4 mentally.
WorkedExamples.Method: Use multiplication facts for 4 and place-value decomposition.

WorkedExamples.Title: Original group 2: all 10 fraction positions
WorkedExamples.Question: Label fractions 1/2 to 10/2 on the same unit-scaled number line. Which are whole numbers?
WorkedExamples.Method: Use 1/denominator equal intervals; integer positions occur when numerator is a multiple of denominator.
Steps: Draw 0-to-1 as one complete unit and repeat across to 5.
Place the 10 successive 1/2 increments.
The whole-number points are 2/2=1, 4/2=2, 6/2=3, 8/2=4, 10/2=5.
WorkedExamples.Check: Each numerator at an integer position is divisible by its denominator.

WorkedExamples.Title: Locate one and two from source 1/2
WorkedExamples.Question: The provided number line labels zero and 1/2. Where are 1 and 2?
WorkedExamples.Method: Copy the length of one equal unit fraction rather than assuming the right endpoint is 1.
Steps: Use the gap from 0 to 1/2 as ONE fractional interval.
Repeat 2 equal gaps to the point 1.
Repeat 4 equal gaps total to the point 2.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Return only the simplified equivalent fraction names instead of labeling all 31 source fractions.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The source has three distinct group-assigned number line lists with 31 tasks.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Preserve every term and compare aligned whole points.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Mark a whole number only when the numerator equals the denominator.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Test numerator divisible by denominator, not only equality.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Assume one is already marked on Activity 2 number lines.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Each source graphic supplies ZERO and a unit fraction; the target 1 is missing.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Iterate the given fractional length d times to reconstruct one.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Draw 1/8 units at a different spacing after locating 1.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The source asks extending the same length scale through 2.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Repeat identical equal units across the entire number line.

SummaryPoints: Original group lists: 10 halves, 9 thirds, 12 fourths, 31 located fractions total; 11 fraction names align with whole numbers.
A whole number n can be represented as n×d/d. Original lines compare halves, thirds, fourths.
Original four Activity 2 unit-fraction landmarks are 1/2,1/4,1/6,1/8; locate 1 with 2,4,6,8 matching steps and 2 with 4,8,12,16.
Three-pupil group labels and teacher explanation remain human-reviewed, as do true equal-length constructions.
Original 2021 source artwork and teacher-gated assessment are not copied; student task PDF and Stage D/test execution not certified.
